These leaders become the unofficial shock absorbers: fixing what’s broken, mediating conflict, and maintaining performance when others are distracted or disengaged.

Over time, reliable executives get pulled into three roles: buffer, fixer, and translator. Each feels like leadership; however, each becomes a liability.

Your nervous system cannot tell the difference between a demand your boss gave you and a goal you set yourself.

In AuDHD brains with a PDA profile, the amygdala runs continuous autonomy threat detection across every obligation regardless of origin. When a task shifts from wanted to expected, dopamine dysregulation kills the reward signal and threat circuitry activates in its place. The prefrontal cortex, already under resourced, cannot override it. Avoidance follows and then shame consumes whatever executive function remained. The spiral is a resource allocation problem running on a nervous system that learned compliance was dangerous and never got updated.

Most people with this profile spent years believing they were the obstacle. The business they could not build, the routine they could not hold, the relationships they kept complicating…all of it traced back

Это конечно не полный список того, что можно посмотреть в Нижнем, но это, на мой взгляд, самые интересные и уникальные места, которые вот точно пропускать не стоит!

Ингредиенты:

• Чечевица — 200 г
• Греческий йогурт — 110 г
• Яйца — 2 шт
• Масло гхи (или оливковое / авокадо) — 1 ч.л.
• Разрыхлитель — 5 г
• Соль — 5 г
• Специи — по вкусу
(у меня: сушёный чеснок + молотый кориандр)
• Семечки тыквы и кунжута — для посыпки

⸻

Как готовить:

1️⃣ Замочить чечевицу в холодной воде на ночь
2️⃣ Утром слить воду и промыть
3️⃣ Добавить йогурт, яйца, масло, соль, разрыхлитель и специи
4️⃣ Пробить блендером до кашеобразной массы
5️⃣ Переложить в смазанную форму
6️⃣ Посыпать семечками
7️⃣ Выпекать при 180°C ~ 40–50 минут до сухой шпажки

Как на вкус? Вкусно! 
Главное добавьте соль и любимые специи/сушеные травы. Иначе такой хлеб покажется пресным. 
Легкий вкус чечевицы можно почувствовать только если есть этот хлеб в «голом» виде. Для этого обязательно замачивайте чечевицу на ночь, а с утра очень хорошо промойте чистой водой.

Выбирать и решаться правда тяжело, но необходимо.

Часто люди смотрят на выбор как на волевой акт — что-то, что нужно создать усилием.

Это может быть и так, но часто выбор просто вызревает и естественно происходит, если внутри себя я примирилась с этими 5 вещами из видео.

Вот они по порядку:
1. Я не могу выбрать всё везде и сразу. Не могу. Часы в сутках и годы моей жизни ограничены, когнитивные ресурсы тоже. Признавать свою ограниченность страшно и не хочется.

2. Выбираем мы всегда либо себя, либо других. Каждое решение о реализации и выражении себя — это решение, которое кого-то может ограничить. Мы все влияем друг на друга, от этого никуда не деться.

3. Мы контролируем только свои действия. А других — нет. Мир тоже нет. Что будет после моих действий, я предсказать не могу. И неопределённость — это тоже страшно.

4. Никто кроме меня не сделает выбор. Я в этом одна и полностью ответственна за себя. Снова страшно. Ну, и одиноко. Большая мама не придёт, и мне придётся как-то самой.

The clip humorously captures a common workplace reality using a cinematic sci-fi reference. It begins with the text “When something actually needs to get done at work, so you summon the most competent employees,” setting the tone for the joke. Visually, it shows a dramatic sequence where a serious-looking character emerges, followed by a high-tech system activating and assembling a team—almost like elite operatives being called into action.

As the scene progresses, multiple skilled individuals in glowing suits line up, ready for a mission, symbolizing the “top performers” in an office. The contrast between everyday work chaos and this intense, heroic summoning creates the humor—implying that only when things get critical do companies rely on their most capable employees, treating them like a special task force.

@hackyourhr 🦒 Part 6 in my series on how to get promoted this year is about disagreeing productively. 

If you want to move up, you can't avoid conflict. A (very) common weakness I see in general is not being able to disagree - we are by nature avoidant of discomfort. You have to learn how to challenge ideas without challenging authority. 

There’s a Harvard Business Review piece called “How to Disagree with Someone More Powerful Than You” and the core idea is simple: power dynamics change how your message lands. So when your boss makes a call you believe will hurt the business, most people either stay quiet or bluntly say they disagree. 

Neither of those approaches builds trust. The better approach is more strategic. 

First, decide if it's worth speaking up. If the risk to the business is bigger than the risk to your ego, you say something. Second, ask permission to engage: “Can I pressure test that with you for a minute?” This language signals that you're on the same side as your b

The best way to give an update to leadership so they remember you positively.

And here's what separates the people who get promoted from the people who get forgotten.

When leadership asks for an update, most people dump information.
"We did X, then Y happened, and now we're working on Z."
Leaders don't remember data. They remember clarity.

Start with the outcome, not the activity.
Right way: "We're on track to reduce client onboarding from 14 days to 7."
Wrong way: "We've been working on the new client process for three weeks."

Use this exact structure:
"Here's where we are. Here's what informed that. Here's what happens next."

That's it. Three sentences.

"We're moving forward with vendor A.
They beat the others on speed and cost by 30%.
Contract goes out Friday."

You gave them the outcome. The reasoning. The timeline.

They don't need more. They need those three things in that order.

If your pitch isn’t landing with your boss, the problem might not be your idea. It might be your approach.

Research by Gary A. Williams and Robert B. Miller identified five distinct decision-making styles after studying 1,600 executives. And each type requires a completely different pitch strategy.

The five decision-maker types:

- **Charismatics (25%)** – Enthusiastic about new ideas but ultimately decide based on balanced information. Don’t confuse excitement with approval.
- **Thinkers (11%)** – Analytical, methodical, and risk-averse. They need detailed data and structured arguments.
- **Skeptics (19%)** – Challenge everything, especially ideas that conflict with their beliefs. Address objections directly.
- **Followers (36%)** – Rely on precedent and trusted opinions. Show proof and examples of others who’ve said yes.
- **Controllers (9%)** – Dislike uncertainty and want ownership. Give them facts and space to decide.

Strategic Planning vs Tactical Planning vs Operational planning... what’s the actual difference? 

Most plans fail because they mix three very different types of planning.

Strategic planning:
Defines the long-term direction of the business over the next 3–5 years, forcing leaders to choose a small number of priorities and make the hard trade-offs about what the company will and won’t pursue.

Tactical planning:
Translate that strategy into concrete initiatives over the next 1–3 years, assigning clear ownership to projects that move the strategy forward.

Operational planning:
Focuses on the daily and weekly execution that keeps the business moving, turning plans into repeatable actions and measurable results.

When you separate these three layers properly, it helps everyone understand and implement the vision properly and progress accelerates.

So here are 8 things to tell yourself before bed if you want to retrain your brain instead of reinforcing stress.

1. Today is complete.
 
  Your nervous system needs closure. Completion reduces cognitive looping.
 
2. I did enough.
 
  Perfectionism keeps threat circuits active. Safety shuts them down.
 
3. One moment does not define me.
 
  Social threat weighs heavier than task success. Release the one comment.
 
4. My brain can rest now.
 
  Your prefrontal cortex has been on duty all day. Give it permission to power down.
 
5. I don’t need to solve tomorrow tonight.
 
  Rumination feels productive but it burns fuel without resolution.
 
6. My body is safe.
 
  Safety is the signal that allows deep recovery.
 
7. I am allowed to grow without urgency.
 
  Neuroplasticity works through repetition, not panic.
 
8. The life I want is built through small aligned decisions.
 
  Change happens at the neural level, not through force.
 Your brain consolidates emotional memory during sleep.

thebodybuildingdietitians Peanut butter is a great source of protein.

You still hear phrasing like this often in the nutrition space, which is exactly why looking at protein in relation to calorie density is so important. When you assess how much protein a food provides relative to the energy it costs, it quickly becomes clear which sources are more efficient.

Peanut butter contains protein, but the amount delivered per calorie is relatively modest. Nuts and seeds more broadly provide protein alongside valuable fats and micronutrients, yet they sit high on the calorie axis. Using them to drive protein intake alone can substantially increase total energy intake.

In contrast, foods such as chicken breast, white fish, lean red meat, egg whites, low fat yoghurt, and skim milk cluster in the lower calorie, higher protein region of the graph.
